coreRootsReason: Core is the code that must stop knowing a provider. integrations/ is where the names belong. scripts/ is release and gate tooling, and the Arthur tenant repository it names is not the Arthur provider. changelog/ and docs/ are prose about what shipped. apps/*/drizzle holds applied migrations, which are history and cannot be rewritten.
excludeReason: A test cannot create production coupling: it exercises core code that still names a provider, and it changes with its subject when S8 to S12 move that provider out. Listing each of the several hundred of them would churn on every test edit and get this gate switched off. Generated files are the output of core files that are themselves scanned, so a name reported twice would be fixed once. The test-support modules and directory, workflow-graph-suites, mcp-dogfood, fixture files and fixtures trees are test material by another name: nothing outside a test imports them, and a fixture naming a provider is the subject of the test rather than a coupling in the product.

jira.reason: Jira becomes integrations/jira, and the ticket lifecycle runs on the issue_tracker capability

plannedIntegrationsReason: A name core still writes, with the stage that takes it away. The gate watches these as well as the ids the registry holds, so it passes on what is here today and fails on anything new. When the stage lands, its id arrives from the registry, this entry and its allowlist rows go, and the gate says so if they do not.
incidentalReason: A row may carry "incidental": true when its files spell a provider id by accident, such as a CSS keyword or a URL, rather than depending on the provider; the gate then keeps the row listed but never reports it as stale, because such a hit comes and goes with ordinary edits and a failure on one could not be acted on.

allowlist.reason: the analysis comment marker (`Arthur report: <run>:<stage>`) and the two headings of the comments it marks (`Arthur research complete`, `Arthur pull requests ready`), all written into tickets and all naming the Arthur tenant rather than the Arthur provider. The marker is a stored identifier in comments already posted, so rewriting it would make the product post a second copy of every report; the headings are what that tenant's people read at the top of those comments, and changing them is a product decision rather than a refactor

the SHAPES of GitHub credentials (`ghp_`, `gho_`, `github_pat_`), named so a token is redacted or reported wherever it turns up: in an unpushed diff, in a sandbox transcript, in an MCP result, in a repository URL somebody pasted. A deployment that ships no GitHub integration at all still has to redact a GitHub token a person hands it, so this is not a dependency on the provider and no stage removes it.

the harness skill importer, whose source kind `github` is a value written into `harness_skill_artifacts.source_kind` on every skill imported from a repository, pinned by a CHECK constraint and by the four columns that variant carries, and whose locator is the stored `https://github.com/owner/repo` URL an artifact keeps. Every provider CALL this feature makes now goes through the `RepositorySkillSource` port an integration implements, so the name that is left is the stored identifier and the sentences a person reads about it. Rewriting either would orphan the artifacts already imported, which is a data migration and a product decision, not a refactor.

`GITHUB_BASE_BRANCH` in the frozen list of environment names the worker permanently refuses. The list is deliberately a literal rather than anything derived, so that a later registry edit cannot make a retired name legal again; a retired name has to stay spelled out somewhere, and this is that somewhere.

the producer name `github-actions` on delivery envelopes recorded before `trustedByDefault` was part of the trigger contract. It is read off rows already in the database and never written: a stored envelope carries no bit, and re-deciding trust from nothing would either start runs that could not start before or stop runs that could. New envelopes carry the bit their integration set, so this set answers only for the old rows and can never grow.

the cockpit activity drawer, whose rows are hardcoded sample events (invented pull request numbers, invented tickets) with an invented source label beside each. Nothing here asks which providers are connected, because nothing here reads anything real. The drawer showing fabricated activity to a person is worth fixing on its own, and the provider name is the smallest thing wrong with it.
dashboard screens and helpers that still name the provider; S12 removes them
other worker call sites that still name the provider; S12 removes them
the provider adapters behind the capability ports; S12 removes them

stored identifiers, schema defaults and the provider CHECK constraints; the code moves, and the stored identifiers themselves survive it: rows here going away is not the measure of the stage being done
engine call sites that still name the provider; S12 removes them
provider configuration and credentials read from the environment; S12 removes them
the provider webhook and API routes, which keep their URLs; the code moves, and the URL a provider already calls survives it: rows here going away is not the measure of the stage being done
what a sandbox agent is handed about the provider; S12 removes them
service call sites that still name the provider; S12 removes them
shared contracts, prompts and skills that still name the provider; S12 removes them

the investigate block names the provider as DATA, not as something core talks to: a stored parameter value (providers: ["jira", "slack"]), the parameter keys slackChannels and slackLookbackDays, the editor fields that write them, the resolver rule that reads them, and the built-in templates and historical metadata that carry them. Filip kept investigate in core until S12 (2026-09-20, amending plan decision 17) so two enabled production definitions keep working. S12 splits the block and its parameters become capability-shaped; these rows go with it. Core reaches the messages themselves through the messaging capability and imports nothing of the provider.

the investigate block's stored parameter vocabulary in the shared workflow contract still includes slackChannels and slackLookbackDays. S12 splits investigate and replaces those parameters with capability-shaped values; this exception leaves with them.
the send_slack_message compatibility alias keeps stored definitions and suspended runs working until the explicit rewrite has run and been verified. R1 removes the alias after that verification.

the leak review scans an unpushed diff for the SHAPES of credentials, and it names each shape so the finding a person reads says which kind of token leaked. The pattern would be worth keeping if this product never talked to the provider at all, so it is not a dependency and no stage removes it.
